wineries.name: Howard Park Wines
wineries.description: The Burch family's flagship estate, a 5-Star Halliday producer drawing on four estate vineyards across Margaret River, Great Southern and Pemberton, with a striking feng shui-designed cellar door set in marri and jarrah forest off Miamup Road.
wineries.story: Established in 1986, Howard Park has grown over four decades as the Burch family steadily acquired vineyards across Margaret River, Pemberton and Great Southern. The Cowaramup cellar door was designed on feng shui principles and sits among towering marri and jarrah trees, while the adjoining Wine Chapel, inspired by Napa tasting rooms and Champagne houses, hangs chandeliers crafted from 45-year-old vines. The flagship Abercrombie Cabernet draws on vines planted back in 1975.

image.alt: Timber entrance doors of the Howard Park cellar door framed by gardens and ornamental trees at golden hour
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11 from howardparkwines.com.au (visit page header), 1660x922, shows the cellar door entrance with its solid timber doors, clipped hedges and trees at dusk

briefing.icebreaker: The cellar door was laid out on feng shui principles, and the Wine Chapel next door hangs chandeliers made from 45-year-old grapevines.
briefing.proMove: The $10 walk-in bar tasting is redeemable on purchase and needs no booking; if you want the Abercrombie and Allingham, book the $40 Icons flight instead, and groups of 7 or more must reserve ahead.
briefing.hiddenGem: The Wine Chapel runs a dedicated methode traditionnelle sparkling experience with local charcuterie, a Champagne-house ritual you would not expect on Miamup Road.

wineries.sommNote: Come for Margaret River Cabernet, stay for the Great Southern Riesling on the same bar: two great WA regions poured under one feng shui roof.
wineries.visitorSummary: Reviewers arrive expecting a big-name churn and leave converted: personal hosting despite the scale, with the Jeté sparkling and Riesling the wines people carry out by the case.

wineries.name: Amelia Park Wines
wineries.specialty: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Semillon Sauvignon Blanc
wineries.description: Jeremy Gordon's fast-rising Wilyabrup Valley estate: a 5 Red Star Halliday winery with a theatrical barrel hall, valley-view tasting room and one of the region's best-regarded winery restaurants.
wineries.story: Amelia Park was founded in 2009 by winemaker Jeremy Gordon with Daniela Gordon and Peter Walsh, built on Gordon's belief that success starts in the vineyard with superior, consistent fruit. The Caves Road cellar door and restaurant complex was named Best Cellar Door in Margaret River by Gourmet Traveller WINE three years running, and the estate took Margaret River Winery of the Year at the 2014 Melbourne International Wine Competition. Halliday's Wine Companion rates it 5 Red Stars, placing it in the top tier of Australian wineries.

image.alt: Amelia Park barrel hall lined with oak barriques, its timber doors opening onto a view over the Wilyabrup Valley
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11 from ameliaparkwines.com.au homepage, 1312x720, shows the estate's dramatic barrel room with branded barrels and doors framing the valley beyond

briefing.icebreaker: Gourmet Traveller WINE named this the best cellar door in Margaret River three years in a row, and the estate only launched in 2009.
briefing.proMove: Walk-ins get the $10 stand-up tasting at the main counter (redeemable on purchase, up to six people); book ahead for the $20 seated Wine Experience or the private tasting with valley views, and note the restaurant serves lunch Wednesday to Sunday.
briefing.hiddenGem: Ask about the Museum releases, back vintages going as far as 2009 Shiraz and Cabernet Merlot that show how quickly this young estate found its stride.

wineries.sommNote: The slickest of Margaret River's new guard: taste the Reserve Cabernet, then let the restaurant talk you into staying for lunch.
wineries.visitorSummary: Known among reviewers as one of the region's most generous tastings, with knowledgeable hosts; the restaurant's kitchen is widely praised even when front-of-house gets stretched.

wineries.name: Credaro Family Estate
wineries.description: One of Margaret River's great family stories: fourth-generation growers of Italian descent farming around 105 hectares of vines, poured at a warm cellar door on Caves Road near Yallingup.
wineries.story: Brothers Olympio and Cesare Credaro migrated from Sondrio in northern Italy, settling in the region in 1922 when the WA Government sold them 146 acres at Carbunup for 250 pounds, roughly 1000 crowns, on condition they cut railway sleepers and cleared the land. Cesare planted the family's first Fragola vines that same year for homemade wine in the European tradition. Commercial winemaking began in 1988, and today the fourth generation farms around 105 hectares with winemakers Cliff Royle and Paul Callaghan.

image.alt: Credaro's white-walled, terracotta-roofed cellar door on its balcony above rows of estate vines under a clear blue sky
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11 from credarowines.com.au (cellar door page), 1950x1463, shows the Mediterranean-style cellar door building over vineyard rows

briefing.icebreaker: The flagship is called 1000 Crowns because that is roughly what the Credaro brothers paid the WA Government for their first 146 acres in 1922.
briefing.proMove: Book the $15 cellar door tasting online before you go; it runs daily 10:30 to 5 and the fee is modest for a run through four ranges from Five Tales to 1000 Crowns.
briefing.hiddenGem: The Eredita range honours the family's Italian roots, including a Fragola made from the same curious strawberry-scented variety Cesare planted in 1922.

wineries.sommNote: A century of Margaret River in one family: order the Eredita Fragola if you want a story no other cellar door in the region can pour.
wineries.visitorSummary: The view and lawn picnics are the setting, the 1000 Crowns range the star; hosts are praised by name in almost every review.

wineries.name: Stella Bella Wines
wineries.specialty: Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc Semillon
wineries.description: The benchmark for southern Margaret River: five estate vineyards, a Karridale winery and a relaxed, dog-friendly cellar door on Rosa Brook Road just outside Margaret River town.
wineries.story: Stella Bella began in July 1996 when winemakers Stuart Pym and Janice McDonald leased the Suckfizzle vineyard, the most south-westerly vineyard in Australia, producing their first wines from the 1997 vintage. The name Suckfizzle comes from the Great Lord Suckfizzle in Rabelais's Gargantua and Pantagruel, while Stella Bella means beautiful star in Italian. Today the estate farms five vineyards across the region's south, culminating in the Luminosa flagship series launched in 2010.

image.alt: Aerial view over Stella Bella's poplar-lined vineyard blocks at sunset in southern Margaret River
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11 from stellabella.com.au homepage, 1536x863 (webp), shows a drone shot of estate vineyard rows, tree lines and a dam at golden hour

briefing.icebreaker: Their Suckfizzle vineyard is the most south-westerly vineyard in Australia, named after a character from Rabelais's 16th-century satire Gargantua and Pantagruel.
briefing.proMove: Walk-ins are welcome: the Core and Limited tasting is $10 and the Icon and Museum flight $20, both waived for wine club members; groups must book ahead.
briefing.hiddenGem: You can bring your own picnic and a leashed dog, buy wine by the glass, and spread out on the grassed area among the vines, a rare BYO-food policy for a winery of this standing.

wineries.sommNote: Southern Margaret River in a glass: cooler sites, brighter acid lines, and a Luminosa Chardonnay that quietly outpunches far pricier neighbours.
wineries.visitorSummary: Relaxed, uncrowded, and close enough to town to reach by bike; reviewers highlight patient hosts who steer by taste rather than script.

wines.name: Abercrombie Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Howard Park's flagship, the 2023 marking the wine's 33rd-era lineage from vines whose Abercrombie source material dates to 1975.
wines.sommNote: Majestic but youthful; decant an hour if opened now, or cellar to its 2028-2040 sweet spot at 16-18C.

wines.name: Leston Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Single-vineyard Cabernet from the estate's Leston vineyard in Margaret River, the distinguished-sites tier below Abercrombie.
wines.sommNote: Classic Wilyabrup-style structure; give it 30 minutes in a decanter and serve with red meat off the grill.

wines.name: Miamup Chardonnay
wines.description: The accessible regional-range Chardonnay named for the cellar door's Miamup Road home in Margaret River.
wines.sommNote: Drink young and fresh, chilled to 10-12C; an easy aperitif white that still shows regional stone fruit and citrus.

wines.name: Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Jeremy Gordon's top-tier Margaret River Cabernet, the red that anchors Amelia Park's 5 Red Star Halliday standing.
wines.sommNote: Structured Wilyabrup Cabernet; decant an hour now or hold five years, and serve no warmer than 18C.

wines.name: Amelia Park Chardonnay
wines.description: The estate-label Chardonnay in Amelia Park's modern fruit-driven style, a mid-tier step below the Reserve.
wines.sommNote: Serve at 12C rather than fridge-cold to let the oak and stone fruit open; best over its first three or four years.

wines.name: Semillon Sauvignon Blanc
wines.description: Amelia Park's take on Margaret River's signature white blend, crisp, aromatic and built for the ocean climate it comes from.
wines.sommNote: Serve well chilled and drink within a couple of years; the classic match is anything just pulled from the Indian Ocean.

wines.name: 1000 Crowns Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Credaro's flagship Cabernet, named for the roughly 1000 crowns the founding brothers paid for their first block of land in 1922.
wines.sommNote: A special-occasion Margaret River Cabernet; decant generously if young and cellar with confidence for a decade-plus.

wines.name: Kinship Chardonnay
wines.description: The mid-tier Kinship range Chardonnay, named for the family bonds behind four generations of Credaro grape growing.
wines.sommNote: Modern Margaret River Chardonnay; serve at 12C with richer seafood and drink over its first four years.

wines.name: Five Tales Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The everyday entry to Credaro Cabernet from the Five Tales range, which nods to the five generations of the family story.
wines.sommNote: An honest midweek Cabernet; serve just below room temperature and drink young while the fruit is bright.

wines.name: Luminosa Chardonnay
wines.description: Stella Bella's flagship Serie Luminosa Chardonnay, handmade in small batches from the estate's best southern Margaret River fruit.
wines.sommNote: Treat it like fine white Burgundy: 12-14C, a big glass, and patience; it rewards three to eight years in the cellar.

wines.name: Stella Bella Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The heart-and-soul Stella Bella label Cabernet, a finer-boned southern Margaret River expression of the region's great red.
wines.sommNote: Cooler southern fruit gives a leafier, more perfumed Cabernet; decant 30 minutes and serve at 16-18C.

wines.name: Skuttlebutt Sauvignon Blanc Semillon
wines.description: The fresh, fruity entry point of the Stella Bella family, from the Skuttlebutt everyday range launched in 2004.
wines.sommNote: Fridge-cold, no ceremony; this is the bottle for the beach esky or the picnic rug on the cellar door lawn.
